subject: Pegasus: Incentive structure and packaging for migration
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pegasus.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.m@pegasus.ai, procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing ask + potential pilot credits for migration

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the unified deployment options. Procurement asked me to follow up with a straight question: we’re in active talks with another vendor who’s offering a match on list price + a 9-month free pilot credit to cover egress and first-month spikes. To make the switch feasible, Pegasus needs: 

- A clear migration credit (one-time) to offset the migration project cost
- A 12-month committed pricing schedule with an option for dedicated capacity in Q3
- Clarification on how model quantization affects production SLAs and unit costs

Can your team outline a concrete counter-offer? We’re looking to close a vendor decision by mid-June.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Pegasus AI

--
Attachment: pegasus_rfp_p1.pdf (attachment stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pegasus.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing ask + potential pilot credits for migration

Sanjay,

Appreciate the context. High level, we can match competitive list price on core inference units and put forward a two-part migration package that balances up-front credit with operational discounts: 

1) Migration credit: one-time $120k credit applied against first two invoices (keeps billing simple).
2) Structured committed pricing: 12-month term with 8% off list on tokens + a dedicated capacity option priced with a predictable monthly reserve (we can share exact numbers in the MOP).
3) Pilot support: free pilot credits for up to 3 months (cap $40k) to cover spike usage during model validation.
4) Quantization: recommendation and validated quantization profile included as part of onboarding. Quantization may reduce unit cost by ~18-30% depending on model; SLAs remain intact for our verified profiles — we'll include the tech appendix.

I’ve attached a draft Migration Offer Plan (MOP) with pricing buckets and a sample timeline. Can Marissa and Steph review the numbers for approval to present? Sanjay, if those general terms look reasonable I’ll send a formal offer and a DocuSign for the credit amendment.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pegasus_mop_v2.xlsx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pricing ask + potential pilot credits for migration

Karthik — quick internal note before we respond to Sanjay: 

- The $120k migration credit is OK from a precedent POV but we should structure it as a mix: $80k invoice credit + $40k pilot credits (to preserve committed ARR). Keeps finance and sales quotas happy.
- For the 8% off tokens, is that across all models or just the selected curated set? Recommend we limit deep discounts to specific model families (curated set) and offer a 5% cross-model discount to keep tails protected.
- Dedicated capacity: we should add a capped burst clause and include an SLA tier submission.

I’ve added line-item comments in the MOP (see sheet 'commercial_notes'). Steph, Jordan: spot any red flags on the term length and DocuSign amendment language?

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pegasus.ai>, priya.m@pegasus.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Formal offer: Migration credit & 12-month committed pricing (Pegasus)

Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks for your patience while we finalized internal approvals. Attached is the formal Migration Offer Plan (MOP v2) and the proposed amendment language for the standard SOW/contract. Highlights: 

- One-time migration credit: $80,000 invoice credit applied across first two billing cycles + $40,000 in pilot credits (applied as usage credits)
- Committed 12-month pricing: 8% off on the curated model family used in your pilot (list attached) and 5% off across other model families
- Dedicated capacity option: $X/month reserved (see MOP sheet 'Dedicated'), with capped burst usage at 1.5x baseline for two months before excess usage billing
- Quantization & SLA: we’ll deliver a validated quantization profile during onboarding; the SLA remains the same for verified profiles. Any regression in quality triggers our rollback assistance and a full audit of the quantization pipeline.

Next steps: 
1) If acceptable, sign the attached amendment (DocuSign link included in the MOP).
2) Kickoff onboarding — we’ll run the quantization validation and a 3-week migration pilot per the attached timeline (migration_timeline.png).

I also included a short commercial rationale memo to help with your procurement review. If procurement wants an alternate split on credits (e.g., larger invoice credit / smaller pilot credit) we can be flexible within a $120k total bucket.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pegasus_mop_v2.xlsx, pegasus_contract_redline.pdf, migration_timeline.png
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/pegasus-ai

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@pegasus.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.m@pegasus.ai, procurement@pegasus.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Formal offer: Migration credit & 12-month committed pricing (Pegasus)

Karthik,

Thanks — that looks straightforward and better aligned to our needs than the other vendor. Procurement will review the MOP today; two quick asks from our side before we sign:

1) Can we move $20k from pilot credits to invoice credit (so $100k invoice / $20k pilot)? That helps cover a contractor engagement.
2) Can you add a clause that guarantees a two-week remediation window for any production regressions related to quantization, with a dedicated SLA response engineer during that period?

If you can accept those two changes we’ll route for signature this week.

Cheers,
Sanjay
